The final deletion transaction locks the app, rechecks mobile revocation, locks and snapshots every current frontend row, then deletes the app and cascades those rows. Only its acknowledged return authorizes object deletion. The app foreign key serializes inserts with deletion; deployment locks serialize publication with the snapshot. Activation and final deletion acquire the same parent app row lock before deployment rows; a missing parent rejects activation.

No general TypeScript refinement, live R2 proof, arbitrary object counts, account authorization, account deletion, cache consistency, pending object uploads, crash orphan collection or concurrency of unrelated teardown providers.
